title: Node lander self-heals a dirty runtime-metadata tree instead of looping BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE
description:
MEASURED LIVE (UnAI, 2026-09-17): goal-b2cc3b54's FIRST node.deliver looped ~5 min refusing REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE. Root cause: the node lander's baseline() (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts:128-141) calls git.observe(workspace) and returns null the moment ANY entry is dirty, logging e.g. `[lander] <node>: TRACKED_RUNTIME_METADATA_DIRTY (1 tracked runtime metadata path(s) changed: [".moe-next/start.ps1"] ...)`. node.deliver then refuses BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE and the wrapper auto-retries FOREVER ("automatic retry after <ts>") until a human checkpoints the tree. It only unblocked when the operator manually `git commit`ed the one dirty path.

The dirty path was `.moe-next/start.ps1`, edited earlier this session to add `--operator-stdin`. Two compounding facts:
1. `.moe-next/start.ps1` is TRACKED, yet `.moe-next` is in .gitignore — a tracked file inside an ignored dir. The runtime-metadata git-exclude work (PR#46 era) never `git rm --cached`ed it, so any edit to it dirties the tree.
2. The lander treats a dirty tracked runtime-metadata path as a hard baseline refusal, with no self-heal — so a routine operator edit to a runtime file wedges ALL node execution behind a human.

OWNER DIRECTION (2026-09-17): "instead of the dirty cycle, the node should commit what's needed or stash." i.e. the lander should checkpoint/stash the dirty RUNTIME-METADATA paths itself rather than park behind a human.

DELIVERABLE OPTIONS (plan the leanest; likely BOTH — prevention + defense):
- (a) DEFENSE: before refusing, the lander auto-checkpoints (commit) or stashes dirty paths that are on the RUNTIME-METADATA allowlist only, then re-observes and proceeds. Scope is the crux: it must NEVER auto-commit product code — only the known runtime-metadata set (.moe-next/ runtime files). A dirty PRODUCT path must still block (that dirt is the operator's real work).
- (b) PREVENTION: untrack the runtime-metadata files that should not be in product history (`git rm --cached .moe-next/start.ps1` and siblings; keep them gitignored) so they never dirty the tree. Verify which .moe-next/* paths are tracked-but-ignored across a fresh project and the fixtures.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING: what git.observe/the lander classifies as "tracked runtime metadata" (the allowlist), where that set is defined, and whether option (b) alone removes the class of dirt or the lander can still see other tracked runtime paths dirty.
definitionOfDone: A dirty TRACKED RUNTIME-METADATA path (e.g. an edited .moe-next/start.ps1) no longer wedges node.deliver: the lander either checkpoints/stashes it and records the baseline, or the path is untracked so it never dirties the tree. Verified against the exact live repro (edit start.ps1, claim a node, confirm BASELINE_RECORDED not BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE).

Scope fence proven: a dirty PRODUCT-CODE path STILL refuses the baseline (BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE) and is NOT auto-committed. Test asserts both arms — runtime-metadata dirt self-heals, product dirt still blocks — with the exact reason code/layer (global rail: assert the code, not just outcome).
If option (b): enumerate the .moe-next/* paths that are tracked while .moe-next is gitignored and untrack the runtime-metadata ones; confirm a fresh project bootstrap does not re-track them.

No infinite-retry stall path remains for the runtime-metadata dirty class: the wrapper reaches a delivered/executing node or a DISTINCT actionable refusal, not an endless REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE loop.

(c) `sed -n '128,141p' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts` -- confirm gate B returns null on `!observed.ok` OR `entries.length !== 0`. (d) In the LIVE project: `git -C D:/projexts/UnAI ls-files -- .moe .moe-next` and `grep -n moe D:/projexts/UnAI/.gitignore`. RED then GREEN -- make the dirty metadata paths machine-readable. In apps/daemon/src/repository/git-landing-port.test.ts first ADD a failing arm: the TRACKED_RUNTIME_METADATA_DIRTY refusal carries `paths` equal to the EXACT, FULL, sorted list of dirty tracked metadata paths -- assert the literal array for a small case, and for the existing 20-path fixture at line ~58 assert `paths.length === 20` so the truncation that limits `detail` to four entries is proven NOT to limit `paths`. Confirm RED. Then in apps/daemon/src/repository/git-landing-port.ts widen the refusal variant at :36 to carry `readonly paths?: readonly string[]` and populate it at :157 from the already-computed `metadata` array, sorted, UNTRUNCATED and UNSLICED. Leave the `detail` string byte-identical -- git-landing-port.test.ts:60 asserts `"20 tracked runtime metadata path(s)"` and node-lander-tracked-metadata.test.ts:59 asserts the code appears in a detail string; both must stay green untouched. The field is ADDITIVE so every existing toMatchObject still passes; confirm that by running the three consumer test files named in planningNotes insight 6. Keep this file at or below its current 257 lines -- it is already over the 250 target, so add the field and nothing else.

The self-heal, as a NEW focused module so neither existing file grows past its cap. Create apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts exporting one function, roughly `checkpointRuntimeMetadata({git, workspace, nodeRef, paths, clock}): Promise<{outcome: string; detail: string; ok: boolean}>`. Behaviour: (1) refuse `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_PATHS` if ANY supplied path is not classified as Moe runtime metadata -- this is the SCOPE FENCE and it must be enforced HERE, in production, not merely relied upon from the caller. Do NOT reimplement the classifier: export `isMoeMetadata` from git-landing-port.ts and import it, so the fence and the observer can never disagree (global rail: a property is asserted against the production surface, never a helper that reimplements it). (2) Call the EXISTING `git.commit(workspace, paths, message)` -- never write new git plumbing; it already stages by explicit nul-delimited pathspec under LANDER_IDENTITY, which is what keeps epic rail 3 (no `git add -A`, no stash, no reset) satisfied. Owner direction was "commit what's needed or stash": COMMIT is chosen and STASH is forbidden by epic rail 3, so a stash path must not be written. (3) Commit message names what happened and why in plain words -- that the node runtime checkpointed pre-existing runtime-metadata changes so execution could proceed, naming the node -- because this commit lands in the OPERATOR'S history and must be self-explaining and revertable. (4) On commit failure return `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED` carrying git's stderr tail. (5) Re-observe; if metadata is STILL dirty return the DISTINCT `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_INEFFECTIVE` rather than looping -- a silent re-loop here would just relocate the bug. On success return `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED` carrying the count and the commit sha. Never log or embed a credential. Also create the one-line bridge apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.js containing exactly `export * from "./runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts";` -- the orchestrator directory has 94 such bridges for 96 sources and an import will not resolve without it.

Unit-test the new module against a REAL git repository in a temp dir (the repository tests already work this way -- copy that fixture style rather than mocking git, because the whole defect lives in git's actual behaviour). In a NEW apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.test.ts assert each outcome by its EXACT code, never merely ok/not-ok: (1) a dirty tracked `.moe-next/start.ps1` yields RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED, HEAD MOVED, the working tree is clean for that path, and the commit's author is Moe (from LANDER_IDENTITY) rather than the operator -- so history shows plainly who wrote it; (2) passing a path outside the metadata classification yields RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_PATHS and HEAD IS UNCHANGED and `.git/index` is byte-identical -- this is the fence's own unit arm and it must prove NO EFFECT, not just a refusal; (3) a commit that cannot succeed yields RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED carrying git's own words. Mutation-verify arm (2), which is the load-bearing one: back up runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts to %TEMP%/moe-task-027dda26-runtime-metadata-checkpoint-<workerId>.ts recording its SHA256 (task id in the path, per the drill rail), delete the fence check, confirm arm 2 goes RED, restore by copying the backup back, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a command SEPARATE from the restore. The file is new and therefore untracked, so `git diff` is blind to it and is NOT valid restore proof here. Record both hashes in the step note.

Wire the self-heal into gate A only. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts baseline() (:128-141): when `observe` refuses with code TRACKED_RUNTIME_METADATA_DIRTY AND the refusal carries a non-empty `paths`, call checkpointRuntimeMetadata with those paths, log `[lander] <nodeRef>: <outcome> (<detail>)` in the existing one-line format, and on success RE-OBSERVE and fall through to the normal path so a BASELINE_RECORDED is written and the node spawns. On any non-success outcome log that DISTINCT code and return null as today -- the operator then sees an actionable line naming the repair instead of an opaque BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE repeating forever (DoD item 4). ATTEMPT THE CHECKPOINT AT MOST ONCE PER UNCHANGED DIRTY PATH-SET per node: the wrapper retries this call on a timer, and re-running a failing commit against the operator's repository every few seconds would turn one bug into a write storm. DO NOT TOUCH GATE B: `entries.length !== 0` must still return null and still log BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY, because that branch is ordinary PRODUCT dirt and auto-committing the operator's real work is exactly what DoD item 2 forbids. Keep this file under 250 lines (199 now) -- if the branch does not fit in a handful of lines, move more of it into the checkpoint module rather than growing this one. Do not change node-lander.ts:195: the lander's LANDING-time handling of the same code is a different moment with a different answer and is out of scope.

Invert the live-repro test and add its opposing arm. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts the existing case at :170-192, "refuses tracked runtime metadata dirt before any seat or baseline write", IS the live repro and currently asserts the behaviour this task removes -- BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE, starts===0, HEAD unchanged, `.git/index` byte-identical. REWRITE IT DELIBERATELY, renaming it to say it now CHECKPOINTS that dirt and proceeds, and assert: `result.ok` is true, `starts === 1`, `readLatestLandingBaseline` is NON-null, the log contains RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED and BASELINE_RECORDED, HEAD MOVED, and the new commit touches ONLY `.moe-next/start.ps1` (assert the committed path list, not just that a commit happened). State in a comment on that test WHY the old assertions were inverted -- they encoded "Moe never writes the operator's history unasked", and the owner's 2026-09-17 direction narrowed that to "except for runtime metadata, which otherwise wedges every node behind a human" -- so a future reader sees a recorded decision, not a weakened gate. Then ADD the opposing arm required by DoD item 2, modelled on the product-dirt case already at ~:160: with a dirty PRODUCT file (and no metadata dirt), assert the exact code REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE, `starts === 0`, the log contains BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY and NOT RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED, HEAD UNCHANGED and `.git/index` byte-identical -- the operator's real work must be provably untouched. Add a third arm for the MIXED tree (metadata dirt AND product dirt together): the metadata is checkpointed, the product dirt still refuses with BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE, and the product file is still dirty afterwards. The mixed case is the one a naive fix gets wrong, so it is not optional.

GATE AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. (A) Run, as ONE command, reading the OUTPUT and not the exit code: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/repository/git-landing-port.test.ts src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.test.ts src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts src/orchestrator/node-lander-tracked-metadata.test.ts`. A leg with no `Test Files N passed` count line RAN NOTHING and is not a pass -- a bad filter prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0. Quote the count line. (B) Then the apps/** regression explicitly, because the root vitest include has NO apps/**, so `pnpm test` would prove nothing here: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, count line quoted. Attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline rule -- repo-wide failures at your merge-base, at HEAD, the delta intersected with this task's owned paths -- and report foreign red verbatim rather than hiding it or claiming a green you did not get. (C) ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW on this diff: Can any path reach `git.commit` that is not runtime metadata -- including via symlink, a `..` segment, or a Windows case alias such as `.MOE-NEXT/`? Does the classifier the fence uses agree with the classifier `observe` uses, or did a copy creep in? What happens on a detached HEAD, on an unborn branch with no commits, mid-rebase, or with an index.lock held by another process -- coded refusal or raw throw? What happens when two nodes checkpoint the same workspace concurrently? Does the once-per-unchanged-path-set guard actually prevent repeated commit attempts under the wrapper's retry timer, and does it correctly RE-ARM when the dirty set changes? Is the resulting commit revertable by an operator with one `git revert`? Record each answer in the completion record. (D) Re-run the mutation drill from step 4 if you touched the fence after step 4, and disclose in the completion record that DoD item 3 (option (b), untracking) was measured NOT APPLICABLE, quoting the `git ls-files` and `.gitignore` output from step 1(d) as the reason -- do not leave a DoD item silently unaddressed.

reopenReason:
DoD 1 FAILS in the live configuration. Every project started through the stack host carries `/.moe/` and `/.moe-next/` in .git/info/exclude: prepareRuntimeMetadataExcludes (runtime-metadata-excludes.ts:103-107) writes them at `moe init` and on every host start (project-stack-host-main.ts:311), and the host refuses to start unless .moe-next/wrapper.log is effectively ignored. Measured: D:/projexts/UnAI/.git/info/exclude lines 8-9. Under that exclude, plain `git add` of a TRACKED path exits 1 ("The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: .moe-next") while still staging it (git 2.54.0.windows.1; modified and deleted paths alike). GitLandingPort.commit maps add exit!=0 to GIT_COMMIT_FAILED (git-landing-port.ts:195-196), so the checkpoint returns RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED, baseline() returns null, node.deliver still refuses REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE and the once-per-set guard parks it behind a human: the pre-fix behaviour, relabelled (DoD 4). The row's tests are green only because neither fixture writes the exclude.

DRILL, zero on-disk mutation (temp vitest config in %TEMP%, in-memory transform adding the two exclude lines inside dirtyTrackedMetadata): control -> Tests 2 passed; drill -> Tests 2 failed, the inverted live-repro arm (result.ok false) and the mixed-tree arm; lander log `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED (git could not commit 1 runtime metadata path(s) [".moe-next/start.ps1"]: ...`. Full evidence, fence probes and foreign-red attribution in my row comment.

Re-run: 4-file gate `Test Files 4 passed (4)` / `Tests 52 passed (52)`. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` -> `13 failed | 732 passed (745)`: all 17 failures FOREIGN, from commit 20896d47 (see comment); no owned file among them.

comments.content:
FOLLOW-UP ITEM for the epic-final hardening row (recorded as a comment per the DELIVERY BIAS rail, not filed as a new row).

DETACHED-HEAD CEILING IN THE RUNTIME-METADATA CHECKPOINT. Measured 2026-09-18 with a throwaway probe against the delivered module (probe run out of tree under %TEMP%, deleted; no probe file entered the repo):

  unborn-branch          : RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED ok=true  (commits the repo's first commit, branch=main)
  detached-head          : RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED ok=true  branch reported as "HEAD"
  mid-rebase-conflict    : RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED ok=true  (rebase leaves HEAD detached)
  index-lock-held        : RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED     "fatal: Unable to create ... index.lock" (git's own words, coded, no throw)
  symlink-inside-metadata: RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED ok=true  committed entry is `.moe-next/link` itself; git stores a symlink as its target string and does not follow it, so no product content escapes
  concurrent (2 nodes)   : n1 INEFFECTIVE / n2 FAILED, ONE commit landed, other path left dirty, no throw, no partial commit

THE GAP: on a DETACHED HEAD (which includes an interrupted rebase) the checkpoint commit lands on the detached head, so `git rebase --abort` / a later `git checkout <branch>` would discard it together with the operator's metadata edit. Recoverable from the reflog for 90 days, but not from the branch.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: preventing the write needs a PRE-commit head read, and `GitLandingPort` (apps/daemon/src/repository/git-landing-port.ts:49-52) exposes only `commit` and `observe` — there is no head/branch read. A POST-commit check on `committed.receipt.branch === "HEAD"` is possible today but would not prevent the write, only stop the node proceeding, so it costs lines without closing the gap. Adding the port method is out of this row's scope and per-file cap (git-landing-port.ts is already 257 lines, over the 250 target).

PRECEDENT WORTH NOTING for whoever picks this up: `GitPushResult` at git-landing-port.ts:59-61 ALREADY carries a `DETACHED_HEAD` refusal code, so the codebase already treats a detached head as refusal-worthy on the publish path. The natural fix is a `head(workspace)` read on the port plus a fifth outcome `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_DETACHED_HEAD` refused BEFORE `git.commit`.

NOT A REGRESSION THIS ROW INTRODUCES, for the record: a node was already staffable into a detached-HEAD workspace before this change whenever the tree was clean — baseline() never checked head state. This row's only new exposure is the metadata commit itself landing there. The ceiling is also recorded in the module's own header comment (runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts:21-25) so a future reader sees it in the code, not only on the board.

QA REJECT EVIDENCE (qa-84420029, 2026-09-18). Reviewed completion commit d9855233 (Moe-Task trailer present; task.commits is EMPTY, commitCount 0 - found by trailer). No later commit touches the 7 owned paths; working tree == d9855233 for all of them.

1) LIVE-CONFIG FAILURE (DoD 1, DoD 4). prepareRuntimeMetadataExcludes writes `/.moe/` and `/.moe-next/` into .git/info/exclude at `moe init` (moe-cli-main.ts:131) and before every hosted daemon start (project-stack-host-main.ts:264,311). UnAI .git/info/exclude lines 8-9 carry exactly those. Plain git 2.54.0.windows.1, scratch repo, tracked `.moe-next/start.ps1` edited:
  git add -- .moe-next/start.ps1                          -> exit 1, "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: .moe-next", file STAGED anyway
  printf '.moe-next/start.ps1\0' | git add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul -> exit 1, same
  same for a tracked DELETED path                         -> exit 1
  git add -u --pathspec-from-file=- (same paths)          -> exit 0
  git commit --only <paths> with NO prior add             -> exit 0, commit made
Production module in the same repo (observe -> paths -> checkpointRuntimeMetadata with createGitLandingPort()): observe TRACKED_RUNTIME_METADATA_DIRTY paths [".moe-next/start.ps1"]; outcome RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED, HEAD unchanged, status after `M  .moe-next/start.ps1` (staged).
End to end through createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime: temp vitest config OUTSIDE the repo (%TEMP%), enforce:"pre" transform of repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts that appends, after the anchor `writeFileSync(join(f.workspace, ".moe-next", "start.ps1"), "# existing operator edit\n");`, a write of "/.moe/\n/.moe-next/\n" to .git/info/exclude (anchor throws if absent). Run: -t "checkpoints tracked runtime metadata dirt and proceeds|refuses a dirty product path that sits beside checkpointed metadata". QA_DRILL=NONE -> `Tests 2 passed | 19 skipped`; QA_DRILL=LIVE_EXCLUDE -> `Tests 2 failed | 19 skipped`, "expected false to be true" (result.ok) and the mixed arm missing RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED. Config deleted; nothing written in-tree.
The operator-side note on the live incident already recorded the symptom: the manual `git add .moe-next/start.ps1 && git commit` "silently didn't commit" after a gitignore warning. That was this same exit 1 short-circuiting the &&.

2) FENCE ESCAPES (production module, arbitrary caller, scratch repo with dirty src/product.ts + untracked src/untracked-wip.ts):
  [".moe-next/..\src\product.ts"]   -> INEFFECTIVE, but HEAD moved and committed [src/product.ts] under Moe's identity (git-for-Windows normalises '\' in pathspecs; isConfinedMetadata splits on '/' only)
  [".moe-next/.\..\src\product.ts"] -> same, committed [src/product.ts]
  [":!x/.moe-next/y"]               -> CHECKPOINTED ok=true, committed [.moe-next/start.ps1, src/product.ts, src/untracked-wip.ts] (exclude-only pathspec = everything else)

issues.description: The checkpoint fails in every live project. With `/.moe-next/` in .git/info/exclude, which the host writes before every start, `git add` of the tracked path exits 1. That becomes GIT_COMMIT_FAILED, then RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED, and BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE stays. On git 2.54, `add -u` with the same pathspecs exits 0, and so does `commit --only <paths>` with no add first. Make it succeed under the live exclude. The paths are always tracked, since observe filters out untracked ones.

The live-repro fixture (dirtyTrackedMetadata) and scratchRepository in runtime-metadata-checkpoint.test.ts never write the info/exclude block that every live project carries, so they pass on a setup production never runs. Have the fixtures create it with the production writer (prepareRuntimeMetadataExcludes on the fixture root), not a hand-copied pattern. Keep the existing asserts: CHECKPOINTED, BASELINE_RECORDED, starts===1 and the exact committed path list.

Fence escape through mixed separators. isConfinedMetadata splits only on '/', so `.moe-next/..\src\product.ts` passes it, and Git for Windows treats '\' as a separator in pathspecs. My probe committed src/product.ts, the operator's WIP, under Moe's identity, then reported INEFFECTIVE. `.moe-next/.\..\src\product.ts` does the same. Refuse any path containing '\', and add an arm asserting UNKNOWN_PATHS, HEAD unchanged and a byte-identical index.

Fence escape through pathspec magic. `:!x/.moe-next/y` and `:(exclude)x/.moe-next/y` pass the fence, and git reads them as exclude-only, which means everything else. The probe committed the whole tree, one untracked file included, and reported CHECKPOINTED ok=true. On POSIX, a tracked dir named ':!x' makes this reachable from observe. Refuse paths that start with ':' or commit with literal pathspecs (runtime-metadata-excludes.ts:94 already uses :(literal)), and add arms for both.

The FAILED path has an effect. When git add exits 1 under the live exclude it still stages the metadata path (status after: `M  .moe-next/start.ps1`), and the commit-fault guard arm leaves it staged too. Either leave the index as it was on failure, or assert the index state the FAILED arm leaves and disclose it in the module header. Right now the header says failures are coded, and the change to the operator's index is not mentioned.

The completion record gives the wrong reason for DoD 3. It says `.moe-next/` is NOT wholesale ignored, but that was measured from .gitignore alone. Moe's own exclude writer ignores the whole directory in UnAI (.git/info/exclude lines 8-9), which is the missed premise behind issue 1. N/A still holds, for another reason: the four files are content the operator committed (UnAI `git log -- .moe-next`: 114672e, 2274ba8, fc9832f). Correct the completionSummary.
